D1.title: Clustering dimension
D1.rationale: The two correlation sources named in the registry decision cross-cut and do not nest. The coarsest partition respecting both is their join, which on the Phase 0 fixture is ONE cluster covering the entire panel, where CR2 is undefined and Satterthwaite df collapses to zero. A one-way cluster can absorb one dimension or the other, never both.
D1.covers: anchors reporting in the same period sharing a macro environment
D1.two_way_blocked_because: No multiway CR2 implementation exists anywhere in this repository, validated or otherwise. Standing up an unvalidated one would contradict this project's own treatment of unvalidated inference machinery.

D2.title: Stated residual limitation
D2.must_be_stated_in: every report that carries a HYP-04 standard error
structural_consequences: Cluster count is set by sample DURATION, not universe size. Expanding the anchor universe raises N_events toward the 193 floor while adding zero clusters. Only a longer observation window adds clusters.

Degrees of freedom are single-digit at the gate threshold. Measured on a fixture matching the panel shape 193 events implies (24 quarterly anchors x 8 quarters, approx 192 events): 8 clusters, Satterthwaite df approx 5.7, against 24.5 df under event_id.

D3.title: Covariance estimator
D3.approval_note: Specified is not approved. HYP-01's own artifacts record method_approved false in both GST_HYP01_INFERENCE_IMPLEMENTATION_INVENTORY_v1.0.json and GST_HYP01_R_REFERENCE_VALIDATION_v1.0.json. What exists there is implementation agreement with clubSandwich under preregistered tolerances -- a statement about arithmetic, not a statistical endorsement. HYP-04 inherits that status and claims nothing stronger.
D3.r_validation_does_not_cover: multiway clustering, which is a second independent reason D1 is one-way

D4.title: Finite-sample correction
D4.value: the bias-reduced linearization built into CR2, and nothing else

D5.title: Degrees-of-freedom rule
D5.note: Given D2's second consequence, realized df is the most decision-relevant number this analysis produces after the coefficient itself.

D6.title: Singleton clusters and cluster-count policy
D6.adopted_from: HYP-01 dated amendment 2026-08-16, decisions D8 and D10
D6.new_threshold_requires: a new dated amendment authored without outcome inspection
always_report: raw ICC with its backing cluster count
D6.why_this_pairing_matters: D1 buys conservatism on the standard error at the cost of very few clusters; D6 forbids resolving the resulting thin df by suppression. The obligation falls entirely on disclosure, which only works if the reporting list is mandatory rather than best-effort.

D7.title: Reported lag quantity and its uncertainty
D7.matches_test_invariant: L <= onset_horizon <= L + 2, with 'never earlier than L' as the hard invariant
D7.why_one_sided: The defect is a mechanical bias, not sampling noise. Under an expanding-window target only 1/L of the averaging window is affected at the true onset, so measured |t| thins as the lag deepens and a noisy draw reports onset late. It cannot err early: measured |t| at h < L was 0.71 on the draw where h = L measured 2.08.
D7.does_not_cover: sampling uncertainty, which at the df D2 establishes (approx 5.7 at the gate threshold) is not small
D7.known_imprecision_of_k: k = 2 was measured on synthetic fixtures at specific (L, W) combinations, and dilution grows with L, so a constant k under-covers deep lags and over-covers shallow ones. Fixing k before real data is what prevents it being tuned later.

D8.title: What Stage 2 consumes
D8.rationale: Early tenor costs premium; late tenor arrives after the reaction window it exists to protect against has closed. Given D7's one-sided bias runs late, the lower bound is the only choice that does not compound the known error.

D9.title: Implied volatility promotion

excluded_providers.Alpaca: provider-limitations doc states 'never Alpaca's free indicative options data used as an OPRA benchmark'
excluded_providers.yfinance: serves current chains only; no historical endpoint

D9_1_qualifying_provider.other_provider_requires: a new dated amendment, and arrives with no validation history here

D9_2_per_peer_coverage_floor.why_ceiling_is_stated: flooring would silently double the tolerance

D9_3_universe_floor.applies_to: share of the peer universe clearing D9.2
D9_3_universe_floor.rationale: IV is a secondary/robustness target whose job is comparability with the primary RV analysis. If a small share clears, the IV-eligible subset is liquidity-selected and an RV-versus-IV disagreement becomes uninterpretable -- the target changed and the sample changed together, with nothing distinguishing them.

D9_4_required_lookback_depth.unit: quarters of the anchor sample window
D9_4_required_lookback_depth.why_quarters: so this constraint and D1's cluster count cannot drift apart
D9_4_required_lookback_depth.why_8: The 193-event floor implies approximately 8 quarters of window at 24 quarterly anchors, so the coverage requirement spans the window the analysis actually uses. A shorter lookback would be non-binding: a peer could clear it while carrying nothing for the remaining quarters.
D9_4_required_lookback_depth.also_a_cluster_ceiling: Under D1 the cluster variable IS calendar_period, so Q quarters caps any IV-based analysis at Q clusters. The two cannot be tuned independently.

D9.why_two_floors_not_one_mean: A mean is carried by a handful of deeply covered names and hides exactly the dispersion that matters. The only empirical precedent is the anchor universe, where QuantConnect returned clean historical option pricing for 24 of 24 frozen tickers -- but events per ticker still ranged 1 to 8, median 2. On the most liquid population in this project, per-name depth already varied eightfold, and HYP-04's peers are by construction the thinner names.
D9.stated_tension_recorded_not_resolved: A coverage bar high enough to guarantee comparability systematically excludes the thin small-cap peers plan section 1 says this hypothesis is most interested in. Set high, IV stops being a robustness check on the same population and becomes a different question about liquid names. That is an argument for keeping IV permanently secondary, not for lowering the bar.
always_reported: thinness profile of the IV-eligible subset against the full peer universe

D10.title: Authoritative CR2 implementation
D10.rationale: HYP-01 designates the R / clubSandwich path as authoritative and its Python CR2 as a validated cross-check. HYP-04 has no R path built, so adopting HYP-01's rule verbatim is not literally available. This defers that work to the point where it carries weight -- a confirmatory out-of-sample number -- rather than claiming an authority now that nothing depends on.
constraints: No Phase 3 result may be produced before the R cross-check exists and is reported under preregistered tolerances. Reaching Phase 3 without it is a blocking failure, not a deferrable TODO.
This option is defensible BECAUSE HYP-04 is exploratory and its display gate is closed. Promotion of HYP-04 to confirmatory invalidates the reasoning and requires a new dated amendment.

universe_scope.why_this_is_not_unbounded_drift: Gate condition C3 independently requires the eligible event-ID set to be enumerated and frozen, together with the analysis-code commit, before any result is computed. Whatever universe is in play is pinned at freeze time by the freeze record itself. Permissive scope widens what may be curated; it does not weaken what must be recorded.
universe_scope.consequence_under_D1: Adding tickers adds no clusters. Cluster count is set by window length, not universe width, so extension raises N_events toward the floor without improving degrees of freedom. It buys reach, not precision.
